severity_criteria.source_excerpt: Section 5.1 Inclusion Criteria, criteria 4-8: "Participants are eligible to be included in the study only if all of the following criteria apply:" "4." "IGA score of 3 at screening and Day 1." "5." "EASI score > 7 at screening and Day 1." "6." "Itch NRS score ≥ 4 at Day 1, defined as the average of the 7 days directly before Day 1," "7." "%BSA (excluding the scalp) with AD involvement of at least 10% and up to 20% at" "screening and Day 1." "8." "DLQI score > 10 at screening and Day 1." -- The continuous BSA range is represented as separate lower and upper thresholds. Day 1 is the named assessment time, not a numbered visit, so baseline_visit_number remains null. The protocol describes moderate AD in its title, but does not literally state the schema label moderate_to_severe.

prohibited_concomitant: Any investigational medication other than the study cream (not permitted during screening or the VC/VCE periods)
Topical corticosteroids, calcineurin inhibitors, PDE4 inhibitors, or aryl hydrocarbon receptor-modulating agents (not permitted during screening or the VC/VCE periods)
Other topical agents for treatment of AD, except bland emollients (not permitted during screening or the VC/VCE periods)
Treatment known to affect the course of AD (not permitted during screening or the VC/VCE periods)

Systemic corticosteroids, methotrexate, cyclosporin A, azathioprine, biologic therapies, or other immunosuppressant agents (not permitted during screening or the VC/VCE periods); short-term systemic corticosteroids may be permitted for acute AEs during VCE following medical monitor and sponsor consultation
Phototherapy or tanning beds (not permitted during screening or the VC/VCE periods)
Strong systemic CYP3A4 inhibitors (not permitted during screening or the VC/VCE periods)
permitted_concomitant: Bland emollients except those containing urea, salicylic acid, or lactic acid; continued in the participant's pre-study manner throughout the study, but not within 4 hours before or 2 hours after study cream application
Nonsedating antihistamines; sedating antihistamines on a pre-existing, well-established, stable regimen 2 weeks before Day 1 and throughout the first 8 weeks
Short-term systemic corticosteroids for acute AEs during VCE, with continuation in study or permanent discontinuation of study cream decided in consultation with the medical monitor and sponsor
Over-the-counter nonprescription preparations deemed acceptable by the investigator on an established, stable regimen 2 weeks before Day 1 and throughout the first 8 weeks
Prescription medications, including phytotherapeutic, herbal, or plant-derived preparations, if deemed acceptable by the investigator from 2 weeks before Day 1 through the safety follow-up visit
Ongoing allergen immunotherapy at a stable dose at entry, continued at the same dose throughout the first 8 weeks
Live-attenuated immunizations are not recommended during VC/VCE unless deemed necessary by the investigator
Topical anti-infectives or other topical treatments on active AD lesions are not used within 4 hours before or 2 hours after study cream application
value.population_note: This protocol studies ruxolitinib cream, with separate VC and VCE periods. It requires discontinuation of AD treatments except as outlined in Sections 6.6.2 and 6.6.3. The source does not establish a schema-supported monotherapy or combination-TCS regimen type; restrictions and permissions are stated with their timing and exception above.

background_therapy.source_excerpt: Sections 5.1, 6.6.2, 6.6.3, and 6.6.4, prior/concomitant medications and procedures: "4." "• Participants may use bland emollients (except those containing urea, salicylic acid, or" "lactic acid) such as Eucerin cream." "Participants should continue to use the bland" "emollient/moisturizer in the same manner they did before entering the study and" "throughout the course of the study." "Note: Emollients should not be used within 4 hours before and 2 hours after" "• Short-term use of systemic corticosteroids may be permitted to treat acute AEs" "(eg, asthma) during the VCE period, and the decision to keep the participant in the" "study (or to permanently discontinue study cream) will be made in consultation with" "the medical monitor and sponsor." "• Participants may continue using sedating antihistaminic drugs, as long as their use is" "part of a pre-existing, well-established, and stable treatment regimen, 2 weeks prior to" "Day 1 and throughout the first 8 weeks of study." "There are no restrictions for use of" "nonsedating antihistamines." "• Use of any over-the-counter, nonprescription preparations deemed acceptable by the" "investigator is permitted under an established and stable treatment regimen 2 weeks" "prior to Day 1 and throughout the first 8 weeks of the study." "• Use of any prescription medication (including phytotherapeutic, herbal, or" "plant-derived preparations) within 2 weeks before Day 1 through the safety follow-up" "visit is allowed if deemed acceptable by the investigator." "• Immunizations with a live-attenuated vaccine are not recommended during the" "VC and VCE periods unless deemed necessary by the investigator." "• Allergen immunotherapy (desensitization) that is ongoing at a stable dose at the time" "of study entry may be continued while on study but only at the same dose throughout" "the first 8 weeks of the study." "• Bleach baths are allowed as long as they do not exceed 2 baths per week and their" "frequency remains the same throughout the first 8 weeks of the study." "• Topical anti-infectives or other topical treatments applied to active AD lesions should" "not be used for at least 4 hours before and 2 hours after application of study cream." "The following are not permitted during screening or the VC/VCE periods:" "• Any investigational medication other than the study cream" "• Any of the following topical treatments: corticosteroids, calcineurin inhibitors," "PDE4 inhibitors, or aryl hydrocarbon receptor–modulating agents" "• Other topical agents for treatment of AD (except bland emollients as noted in" "Section 6.6.2)" "• Treatment known to affect the course of AD" "• Systemic corticosteroids, methotrexate, cyclosporin A, azathioprine, biologic" "therapies, or other immunosuppressant agents" "• Phototherapy or tanning beds" "• Strong systemic CYP3A4 inhibitors" -- A permitted exception modifies the general systemic-corticosteroid restriction: short-term use for acute AEs during VCE may be allowed with medical-monitor and sponsor consultation. The prior-treatment washout is not represented as a treatment-period prohibition. This is the posted Protocol Amendment 2, Version 3, dated 08 Aug 2024.

multiplicity_control.source_excerpt: 3.2 Control of Type I Error: "For the coprimary and key secondary analyses, an overall 2-sided Type I error of 0.05 will be" "The following coprimary null hypotheses H1 and H2 will be tested:" "Where 𝑝1 and 𝑝2 are the proportion of participants achieving EASI75 at Week 8 in the" "ruxolitinib 1.5% cream and vehicle cream group, respectively." "The key secondary endpoints will be tested in a fixed sequence as follows if the null hypotheses" "H1 and H2 for both coprimary endpoints (EASI75 and IGA-TS) are rejected:" "• Proportion of participants with ITCH4 from baseline at Week 8" "• Proportion of participants with ITCH4 from baseline on Day 7" "• Proportion of participants with ITCH4 from baseline on Day 3" "• Proportion of participants with ITCH4 from baseline on Day 2" "• Proportion of participants with EASI75 from baseline at Week 8." "• Proportion of participants with IGA-TS at Week 8." -- The SAP states an overall two-sided Type I error of 0.05 for coprimary and key secondary analyses; the four key secondary endpoints follow a fixed sequence only after both coprimary null hypotheses are rejected. The procedure enum serial_gatekeeping represents this stated hierarchy. The SAP does not explicitly state that it was finalized, so finalized_in_sap is null.

study_schedule.source_excerpt: 4.1–4.2 Study Design and Overall Study Duration; Tables 3–4 Schedule of Activities: "Estimated Duration of Approximately 34 weeks: 28 (+ 7) days in the screening period, 8 weeks in the" "Participants will be randomized 2:1 to blinded treatment with ruxolitinib cream 1.5% BID or" "vehicle cream BID for an 8-week VC period." "Following the EOT (Week 24 or ET), all participants will have a safety follow-up visit 30 days" "later (or 30 days after the last application of study treatment if the Week 24 or ET visit was not" "Table 3: Schedule of Activities: Vehicle-Controlled Period" "Days −28 to −1 Day 1c Week 2 Week 4 or ET1" "Table 4: Schedule of Activities: Vehicle-Controlled Extension Period/Escape Arm" "Weeks 12, 16, and 20 Week 24/EOT or ET2 30 Days (+ 7 d) After" "During the VCE period, participants (including those in the escape arm) will have study visits" "every 4 weeks for up to 24 weeks total." "designee will contact the participant in between regularly scheduled clinic visits (eg, Weeks 10," "All participants will have a safety follow-up visit 30 days after their Week 24 or ET visit." "Estimated total duration of participation for an individual is up to approximately 34 weeks:" "28 (+ 7) days in the screening period, 8 weeks in the VC period, 16 weeks in the VCE period," "and 30 (+ 7) days in the safety follow-up period." "14, 18, and 22) to discuss eDiary compliance and to confirm the start and end date of treatment" -- The protocol's full schedule-of-activities tables are present in the cited file. Visit weeks after Week 8 are every four weeks; Weeks 10, 14, 18, and 22 are telephone contacts between clinic visits. Total participation is stated as up to approximately 34 weeks; screening and safety follow-up retain their stated day-based timing. The screening duration of 4 weeks is nominal (28 days) and the protocol allows an additional 7 days.

value.rationale: The protocol calls this response-triggered open-label escape treatment, not rescue therapy. It permits escape to ruxolitinib when EASI50 is not reached at Week 8 or when the response is lost during the extension, with loss confirmed at two consecutive visits at least one week apart.

rescue_therapy.source_excerpt: 4.1 Study Design: "the ruxolitinib 1.5% cream open-label escape arm if EASI50 is not achieved at Week 8 or if an" "Participants will be eligible to enter the ruxolitinib 1.5% cream open-label escape arm" "if EASI50 is not achieved at Week 8 or if an EASI50 response from baseline is lost during the" "VCE period (Note: < EASI50 must be observed at 2 consecutive visits, one of which can be an" "During the VCE period, participants (including those in the escape arm) will have study visits" "every 4 weeks for up to 24 weeks total." "(EASI50 is defined as achieving ≥ 50%" -- The response-triggered open-label escape arm is the protocol-supported treatment escalation represented here. It is not conflated with general concomitant medication rescue; alternative systemic treatment was considered separately by investigators.
